== PLAN PART (1) ASSESSMENT: GATE maybe_auto_hydrate ==

The plan's core fix (gate the v2 file path) is CORRECT. The defect is real and verified. Two refinements needed:

(a) FAIL-CLOSED GATE: The plan says 'gate on hub mode (v3-only)'. Big-pickle correctly identifies that HubMode::resolve degrades to V2 on error (hub_v3.rs:713-718). A hub_mode().is_v3() gate would silently re-enable the destructive v2 path under transient git failure — precisely the concurrent-launch race (catalog 2.2). CONFIRM: gate on v3-REF PRESENCE directly (checkpoint/meta refs exist => skip), not on HubMode. This is fail-closed: if ref detection fails, the v2 path is skipped (conservative), not enabled (dangerous).

(b) AMBIGUITY: 'hydrate only via hydrate_from_state from v3 refs' has two readings. Reading (a) = maybe_auto_hydrates no-ops on v3, hydration via existing mode-gated paths (shared_writer/core.rs:204, locks_cmd.rs:246). CONFIRM: these paths exist and work. This is cheap (no per-command cost). Reading (b) = implement v3 reduce+hydrate inside maybe_auto_hydrate. REJECT: would defeat the sub-millisecond design (main.rs:2286-2288) since compaction::reduce reads ALL agent refs. Plan MUST specify reading (a) explicitly.

== PLAN PART (2) ASSESSMENT: FIX init_cache v2-first ==

Big-pickle's finding 1 is CONFIRMED. The fix is misdiagnosed for three reasons:

1. INERT for ASES: cache already exists (line 170-172 early return). Code change never re-hosts unless re-host logic is added — plan doesn't mention it.
2. HARMFUL for hybrid repos: remigrate-from-v2 reads worktree issues/ files (migrate_hub_v3.rs:746-748, used at 1479). Re-hosting the worktree on v3 host branch hides v2 files from migration.
3. DOES NOT remove wipe source: crosslink/hub-v3-host carries the SAME 4 stale June files (verified via live ASES state). The stale projection follows the re-host.

RECOMMENDATION: Drop (2) from this plan. The v2-first precedence is deliberate migration support (cache.rs:150-157 doc). The defect is that the migration host doubles as ungated auto-hydrate source (fix 1) + write target (fix 3), not the precedence itself.

== PLAN PART (3) ASSESSMENT: STOP trust commits on v2 branch ==

Big-pickle's finding 4 is CONFIRMED. Part (3) covers only ONE of THREE v2-branch writers:
- sync/trust.rs (plan covers this)
- commands/agent.rs:668-690 (agent bootstrap — EVERY kickoff launch)
- commands/swarm/lifecycle.rs:128,200 (swarm archive/reset)

Even with fix (3), every kickoff launch still moves the v2 tip. This is HARMLESS only because fix (1) removes the wipe — but the plan should either widen (3) to all three writers or explicitly accept residual churn as out of scope.

Also confirm finding 5: trust writes to v2 are dead writes for v3 verification (v3 reads from META_REF, which has no allowed_signers in ASES). Stopping them costs nothing today. But there is no runtime path that updates META_REF allowed_signers either — if v3 trust is intended, that is new code and out of scope.

== SURGICAL MITIGATION ASSESSMENT ==

CONFIRM sound. The mitigation (rm -rf .crosslink/.hub-cache/issues) works because:
- read_all_issue_files returns empty for missing dir (issue_file.rs:228-229)
- hydrate_to_sqlite early-returns on empty (hydration.rs:126-128)
- fetch_v2_readonly reset --hard is gated off when v3 (cache.rs:305-311)

Document on #125:
- Restore command: git -C .crosslink/.hub-cache checkout -- issues
- Footgun: restore BEFORE migrate hub-v3 --remigrate-from-v2 (reads those files, migrate_hub_v3.rs:746-748)
- Future v2-mode downgrade re-arms the wipe
- 4 negative-id rows (-1..-4) already persist in DB; acceptance criterion covers only NEW collisions

== VERIFICATION ADEQUACY ==

CONFIRM finding 6: no existing test for maybe_auto_hydrate. grep confirms only hydrate_to_sqlite/hydrate_from_state unit tests. cargo test passing does not verify the gate. Required regressions:
(a) v3 hub + stale v2 files -> auto-hydrate must NOT wipe
(b) V2Only hub STILL auto-hydrates (gate must not break legitimate v2)
(c) Fail-closed: mode-detection error -> skip

== SCOPE DELIMITATION ==

CONFIRM finding 8: #125 is the whole family. State what this plan does NOT fix:
- Catalog 2.3: worktree comment visibility
- Catalog 2.4: uuid-sync quirk
- Catalog 2.2 residual: concurrent explicit syncs both run hydrate_from_state

== THINGS BOTH REVIEWS MISSED ==

1. SYNC COMMAND ORDERING: get_db() is called BEFORE sync_cmd runs fetch. So maybe_auto_hydrate fires BEFORE fetch updates the v2 worktree. The wipe happens with STALE files, then sync's own hydration recovers. This ordering is the mechanism by which the wipe is both triggered and immediately recoverable — worth documenting.

2. fetch_v2_readonly (cache.rs:328-357) resets --hard to remote tip. This would restore the v2 files after a surgical rm. So the mitigation is TEMPORARY — the next sync restores the stale files. But since fix (1) removes the auto-hydrate trigger, the restored files are inert (no one reads them for hydration).

3. The empty-issue early return (hydration.rs:126-128) is a DATA-LOSS GUARD that already exists but is bypassed when the issues/ dir has files (the 4 June-era files). The fix removes the trigger, not the guard.

== OVERALL VERDICT ==

CHANGES REQUESTED.

The plan's mechanism analysis is verified correct. The core fix (1) is essential and correct but needs: (a) fail-closed gate on v3-ref presence (not HubMode), (b) explicit reading-(a) semantics (skip on v3; v3 hydration stays on existing paths). Part (2) should be dropped or re-scoped. Part (3) should be widened to all v2-branch writers or documented as accepting residual churn. Verification needs gate regression tests. Surgical mitigation is sound but needs documentation of restore command, remigrate footgun, and v2-downgrade re-arm.

Fix order: (1) fail-closed gate -> surgical rm -> (3) widen v2-branch writers. (2) should not gate the others. #125 left open.

27980834-49cb-45ce-943c-f01b6ef92132.content: LOCK DESIGN FINDING (2026-08-03, code-verified): locks are NOT fulfilling their blocking purpose due to two gaps. (1) The crosslink-guard plugin (crosslink-guard.ts) NEVER consults the lock table — its active-issue gate reads .active-issue sentinel + session status only; zero references to the lock table. So agent tool calls proceed on issues the lock table says are held by another identity (e.g. OL2r). (2) session work DOES enforce locks (src/commands/session.rs:246-259: enforce_lock + try_claim_lock; bails with 'Lock on #N was claimed by X' if another agent holds it) — but the STALE-detection path makes it bypassable (steal succeeds, or warn-and-proceed when holder looks stale). Root reason staleness can't be trusted: heartbeat hooks not deployed in worktrees (#135 Phase 2 item), so the code defaults to warn-not-block rather than risk blocking a live agent. CONCEPTUAL ISSUE (operator): a lock should BLOCK — currently it warns instead, so it isn't fulfilling its purpose. FIX ORDER: (1) make staleness reliable (deploy heartbeat into worktrees, #135 Ph2) so locks can confidently block/auto-steal; (2) wire the lock table into the crosslink-guard plugin (separate subissue) so the tool gate also respects held locks. Also noted: 18 stale OL2r locks currently — driver-identity locks never released, a cleanup gap. Related: #135, #160, #146.

### Outcome: APPROVE
Independent source re-derivation finds the four r3 items integrate cleanly and preserve the r2 fail-closed boundary:
- **R1 / HIGH confidence:**  now distinguishes absent named remote from confirmed zero remotes;  from  is Forbidden, non-empty enumeration is Forbidden, only confirmed empty is Allowed. 1. **MEDIUM — systemic process reliability:** three builder stalls/silent-hangs occurred on this single r3 lifecycle: T1jj stalled after plan, neHg was position/artifact-silent and was killed, and R99p went silent after commit before final verification. Unit/source evidence supports the verdict, but those live cases remain outside demonstrated coverage.

RESULT — READ-ONLY SYSTEMS/DURABILITY REVIEW of ade6146b (diff vs 4efd9ae6). No files modified, no commit/push; #125 remains open. Targeted gate tests: 3 passed, but coverage is insufficient per findings below.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL / CHANGES REQUIRED. The new local strict probe is directionally correct and fail-closed for the cases it actually observes (spawn failure, broken ref diagnostics, unexpected exit, partial local marker presence). It is not yet a ship-ready system-wide durability gate.

MUST FIX
1. HIGH — remote-only v3 marker fail-open (hub_v3.rs:732-744; hydration.rs:1219-1244). The gate probes exact local refs in the cache repo. If meta/checkpoint exist only as remote-tracking refs (or remote has advanced but fetch/adoption has not occurred), local probes can report both v3 markers absent while local crosslink/hub exists; Ok(true) then runs destructive hydrate_to_sqlite against stale files. This directly violates fail-closed under remote-only-marker doubt. PRECONDITION: gate must consult authoritative remote state, or prove fetch/adoption occurred and treat any remote/local uncertainty as skip; add a regression fixture for remote-only v3 markers.
2. HIGH — bypass callers remain destructive and ungated (tui/mod.rs:534,833). TUI sync completion and startup call hydrate_to_sqlite directly. On a v3 hub they can still import the stale v2 projection and drop agent-authored rows, regardless of maybe_auto_hydrate. Route them through v3 hydrate_from_state / existing mode-gated hydration, or a single fail-closed dispatcher.
3. HIGH — other HubMode gates retain the known fail-open downgrade (hub_v3.rs:780-791; locks_cmd.rs:303; daemon.rs:276-280; shared_writer/core.rs:220-228). Detection error becomes HubMode::V2, which still selects hydrate_to_sqlite. The new helper protects only maybe_auto_hydrate, not these lifecycle paths. Ship requires one fail-closed policy for every v2 hydration entry point, not just the hot path.
4. MEDIUM-HIGH — regression tests do not prove the new primitive. Test (b) is positive by construction: removing the gate still hydrates and passes. Test (c) passes under the old lenient probe as well; it does not discriminate strict_ref_present. Add mutation/discriminating tests: broken marker + checkpoint absent + v2 present must skip under strict and hydrate under the old behavior; make the v2 test fail when gate is removed; include spawn failure/non-git and remote-only cases.

SHOULD CONSIDER
5. MEDIUM — TOCTOU/race: marker comparison, ref probes, and reading issues/ are separate operations (hydration.rs:1199-1247). Two processes can both observe a stale marker; concurrent fetch/worktree reset can change refs/files between probe and hydrate. Serialize probe+hydrate with the hub lock or hydrate an immutable ref/tree snapshot. The marker remains keyed to cache-worktree HEAD, not v3 checkpoint/data refs; this is acceptable only with the explicit reading-(a) contract that v3 auto-hydrate is a no-op and all v3 freshness comes from sync/writer paths.
6. MEDIUM — gate failure policy is silent debug + Ok(false) (hydration.rs:1228-1234). This protects data but can leave stale SQLite indefinitely. Emit observable warning/metric and ensure an explicit recovery path; document that fail-closed means availability degradation.
7. MEDIUM — blast radius/preconditions: if any caller or future caller bypasses the helper, hydrate_to_sqlite's created_by filter can erase agent-authored rows and then advance .last-hydrated-ref (hydration.rs:1244-1247), masking the incident. Enforce a single hydration API and add an inventory test/check for direct destructive callers. Residual v2 writer tip churn (agent.rs:665-680; swarm/lifecycle.rs:93-205; trust.rs:389-620) is harmless only if every destructive entry point is covered.

NIT
8. LOW — helper documentation says “hub mode” but implements a local-ref predicate; name/docs should explicitly state local-vs-remote authority and migration/partial-marker semantics.
9. LOW — comments in agent/swarm/trust document accepted churn but do not make the invariant mechanically enforceable; prefer a central invariant/test over comments.

CONDITIONAL SHIP PRECONDITIONS: (a) eliminate/guard TUI and all HubMode-downgrade v2 hydration paths; (b) close remote-only-marker uncertainty fail-closed; (c) add discriminating mutation tests, including remote-only and spawn/non-repo failures; (d) define locking/snapshot semantics for probe+hydrate and marker freshness; (e) run the full project verification after fixes. Until then: CHANGES REQUESTED, not APPROVE. The gate reduces the original maybe_auto_hydrate exposure but does not establish a system-wide fail-closed durability boundary.

VERDICT (kickoff #207 investigation — crosslink event push to hub failing with gh auth errors). NOTE: issue #207 does NOT exist in the tracker (main DB max id 205; sqlite_sequence=207 shows ids 206/207 were allocated then rolled back — direct evidence of this bug's impact: locally-created issues lost on re-hydration because the hub baseline has only the 4 June-era issues). Posting verdict here on #125, the operator's tracking issue for this exact investigation (SSH test comment 519).

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not hypothesis): PRIMARY failure is a real auth failure — gh has NO stored credential. gh auth status = 'not logged into any GitHub hosts'; ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml is EMPTY (0 bytes). Credential chain: global ~/.gitconfig has credential.https://github.com.helper = (empty) + !/usr/bin/gh auth git-credential (the gh auth setup-git layout). No ~/.git-credentials, no ~/.netrc, no GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN env. gh auth git-credential get returns NOTHING; git credential fill (gh helper only) = 'could not read Username'. So HTTPS push sends no credentials → GitHub 401 'Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported'.

The 'erase operation not supported' in the error is SECONDARY NOISE, not the cause: after the 401, git calls credential erase on the helper chain; the gh helper rejects erase (reproduced exactly: printf ... | gh auth git-credential erase -> 'gh auth git-credential: erase operation not supported', exit 1). Even if erase worked, the push would STILL fail — there is no valid credential. Option (c) (stop erase) fixes nothing.

REPRODUCTION: git push --dry-run blocked by policy; git ls-remote origin HEAD succeeds because the repo is PUBLIC (anonymous read). Read works cred-less; push needs auth and fails. crosslink's push_agent_ref (hub_v3.rs:450) is a plain 'git push' subprocess inheriting the same broken chain.

THE FIX — ALREADY APPLIED AND VERIFIED: at 03:52 the shared .git/config remote.origin.url was switched HTTPS -> git@github.com:rock-solid-sites/ASES.git (operator's comment seq 929 confirms; I observed the change mid-session, did not make it). SSH auth WORKS: ssh -T git@github.com -> 'Hi rock-solid-sites!' (existing ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, repo owner). The operator's test comment (seq 929) PUSHED to origin/crosslink/agents/OL2r — remote now has seq 929. RECOMMENDATION: option (d) switch ASES remote to SSH — cleanest (no token lifecycle, no gh dependency, works headless). Backup: (b) gh auth login --with-token (stores token in hosts.yml; erase noise persists but harmless) or (a) export GH_TOKEN for crosslink env. REJECT (c).

EXACT COMMANDS (operator, main repo — shared config covers all worktrees + hub-cache):
  # verify ssh auth once
  ssh -T git@github.com
  # already applied; if needed on another machine:
  git -C /home/claude-code/projects/ASES remote set-url origin git@github.com:rock-solid-sites/ASES.git
  git -C /home/claude-code/projects/ASES/.crosslink/.hub-cache remote set-url origin git@github.com:rock-solid-sites/ASES.git
  # verify + flush locally-saved events to hub
  git ls-remote origin HEAD
  crosslink sync
Confirmed: hub-cache worktree reads the SSH url from the shared config, and crosslink sync pushes now succeed (origin/crosslink/agents/OL2r advanced 927->928->929 after the switch).

SyncManager::new (sync/core.rs:37-77) resolves HubMode ONCE at construction via local-only HubMode::resolve(cache_dir) (cache absent → V2). init_cache (cache.rs:166-215) takes the v2-first branch whenever has_remote_v2 (the retained remote branch) — it NEVER reaches the v3-join path (fetch_v3_refs_for_join lives only in the no-v2 else-branch) and never flips hub_mode to V3. fetch() (cache.rs:298-320) dispatches on the cached V2 → fetch_v2_readonly (fetches only the v2 branch, no marker adoption). sync_cmd → sync_v2_readonly → hydrate_to_sqlite (4 June-era files). Every subsequent command re-resolves V2 the same way. RESULT: a fresh clone of ASES today is DETERMINISTICALLY stuck in V2 mode — the v3 hub is never joined, sync always yields the 4-issue baseline, and the gate AGREES (local-only) and actively sanctions the v2 path on every marker mismatch (trust commits keep arriving from the main repo). This is the ORIGINAL bug, fully intact, in any fresh environment. hy3 reproduced the probe-level fail-open; the lock-in chain (init_cache branch precedence + cached hub_mode + fetch dispatch) is what makes it permanent and self-sustaining.

A5. TASK (3) — UNGATED TUI EXPOSURE: CONFIRMED + QUANTIFIED. `crosslink tui` is a LIVE advertised command ("Interactive terminal dashboard (read-only)"). Two unconditional hydrate_to_sqlite call sites: tui/mod.rs:833 (startup: init_cache + fetch + hydrate_to_sqlite) and tui/mod.rs:534 (poll_sync — every 30s PERIODIC_SYNC_INTERVAL and after every manual sync; the background thread runs init_cache+fetch only, then poll_sync hydrates with NO hub-mode check and NO gate). Wipe math on a /tmp copy of the production DB: 241 issues, 241 agent-authored (created_by NOT NULL), 0 preserved, and the cache worktree IS checked out on crosslink/hub with the 4 June-era JSON files present → hydrate_to_sqlite's clear_shared_data + created_by-NULL-only preservation → 241 → 4 (100% wipe). The wipe is TIMER-DRIVEN (30s), SILENT (let _ = swallows errors), and REPEATABLE. A user running the read-only dashboard in the ASES main repo destroys the entire issue DB.

A6. TASK (4) — NEW FAILURE MODES (see MUST FIX 2-3, SHOULD CONSIDER 4-7 below).

== PART B — FINDINGS ==

MUST FIX:

1. [MUST FIX — HIGH] Ungated destructive callers outside the diff. The fix gated ONLY hydration.rs:1244 (maybe_auto_hydrate). Still-live v2-path callers:
   - tui/mod.rs:833 + 534 — UNCONDITIONAL, hub-mode-blind. Real-world: `crosslink tui` wipes 241→4 (A5). Highest urgency: a read-only command destroys the DB.
   - locks_cmd.rs:303 (sync_v2_readonly) — gated by hub_mode().is_v3() (line 246) which inherits the HubMode::resolve degrade-to-V2-on-error (hub_v3.rs:709-720, unchanged by the fix): a transient git failure silently re-enables the destructive path — the exact concurrent-launch race class the fix claims to address.
   - daemon.rs:279 — same degrade-to-V2 fail-open, in a long-running process (network/transient failures most likely there).
   - shared_writer/core.rs:220 (hydrate_with_retry) — same pattern; reached by ~20 mutation paths (mutations.rs/milestones.rs).
   - integrity_cmd.rs:379 — v3-aware when v3_state resolves, but falls to the v2 path otherwise (operator-invoked, lower frequency).

2. [MUST FIX — HIGH] Fresh-environment fail-open (A3+A4): gate + mode detection are local-ref-only. On a v3 remote that retains the v2 branch (ASES today), every fresh clone/worktree-bootstrap locks into V2 and the original wipe continues. Recommended directions (for the implementer to design): (a) init_cache joins the v3 hub when the REMOTE advertises v3 markers regardless of a retained v2 branch; and/or (b) the gate probes the remote (ls-remote refs/heads/crosslink/meta) fail-closed (unreachable remote → skip v2 path); and/or (c) delete the remote v2 branch after migration (the retained branch is the trap, kept alive by the trust-publish pushes).

3. [MUST FIX — MEDIUM] Docs overstate the fix. Addendum 04 "RESOLVED 2026-08-06", playbook §6.5 "durable fix", crosslink-fork.md "root cause fixed", and the 12:53 result's "recommend close-worthy for the core guard" — while the wipe remains reachable through 3 routes (TUI, degrade-to-V2, fresh env). Systemic risk: agents will drop the compact-recovery and sequential-launch discipline exactly when the hazard persists. Annotate the RESOLVED marks with the residual scope or hold them until the caller coverage is closed.

SHOULD CONSIDER:

4. Test (b) passes by construction — non-discriminating. The v2-only fixture (setup_git_env_with_v2_cache) yields the same outcome with the gate removed (hydrate runs, issue 7 imported, assert passes). The 11:54 result's claim "all 3 FAIL with the gate removed" is FALSE for test (b). (Reading-proven; corroborates hy3's mutation matrix.)

5. Test (c) does not exercise strict_ref_present's discriminator. The fixture creates BOTH markers then corrupts only meta — checkpoint remains VALID, so strict (Err→skip) and pre-fix lenient (meta collapsed absent, checkpoint present→skip) give the SAME outcome. The novel primitive has zero regression coverage. The discriminating fixture (broken meta + checkpoint ABSENT + v2 present: strict skips, lenient RUNS) must be added — hy3 wrote and verified it; it should be committed.

6. Gate-probe TOCTOU race (fresh-env only, small window): probe-then-act without a lock — a concurrent process creating local markers (bootstrap/join/fetch) between the probe and hydrate_to_sqlite executes a stale decision. Same class as the #123/#124/#137 concurrent-launch race; the fix does not serialize hydration.

7. Marker never refreshed on the gate-skip path: on a v3 hub the marker tracks the V2-branch tip (hub_head_ref = cache worktree HEAD), so every trust/agent/swarm tip move re-triggers the 3-subprocess probe until the next explicit sync. Writing current_ref on the skip path would bound the probe to actual moves. Minor perf; note the probe is otherwise well-behaved (git spawn failure → Err → skip, verified).

NITS:
8. TUI hydration errors are swallowed (`let _ =`), hiding even partial failures.
9. The #427 empty-dir guard is defeated by any single stale file (the 4 June-era files) — pre-existing, reinforced.
10. Old-style v3 refs (refs/crosslink/{meta,checkpoint} without /heads/) are not probed — consistent with classify_hub_version (no NEW divergence), but a v3 layout the gate would treat as v2-only.

== PART C — WHAT PASSED / HONESTY ==

Passed and independently verified: (1) the gate's strict_ref_present semantics (empirical git 2.x behavior: clean-missing=exit1/empty → absent; broken loose ref=exit1+stderr → Err→skip; non-repo=exit128 → Err→skip); (2) the gate placement after the marker check (hot path unchanged); (3) the reading-(a) semantics for the ASES live state (skip, no double-hydration; sync_cmd/daemon/shared_writer v3 paths unchanged and working — my sync hydrated 237 issues via v3); (4) the fix's claim "hub_is_confidently_v2_only returns Ok(false) when v3 marker refs present" — TRUE for the current local state; (5) the writer comments in agent.rs/trust.rs/lifecycle.rs are comment-only (no behavior change). Findings 1-2 of hy3 (ungated callers, HubMode fail-open, remote-only fail-open) and the test-quality findings (b/c) are independently confirmed with additional live evidence; the new contributions are A4 (permanent-V2 lock-in), A5 (quantified timer-driven TUI wipe), A2 (independent live pass), and findings 3/6/7 (docs overstatement, TOCTOU, marker-never-refreshed).

== BOTTOM LINE ==

The gate is a correct and necessary first layer and it DOES protect the current ASES main repo (verified live). It is NOT the durable family fix the docs claim: the destructive v2 path remains reachable via a live read-only command (TUI — 100% wipe), via degrade-to-V2 under transient git failure (locks/daemon/shared_writer), and via every fresh environment of the v3 remote (permanent V2 lock-in, original bug intact). Close the caller coverage (at minimum gate the TUI paths and add remote-probing to mode detection), add the discriminating test (c) fixture and a test-(b) discriminator, and correct the RESOLVED documentation before this is merged/pushed as the durable fix. #125 stays OPEN.

980dadaf-45ef-4253-899d-1992efc16571.content: VERDICT — CONDITIONAL: adopt the watcher for observation/notification, but do not enable autonomous recovery until the controls below are specified and fault-tested. (1) Nudge-first is directionally safer than immediate kill+relaunch because it preserves context and avoids needless token burn, but tmux send-keys is not a reliable recovery primitive: it can target the wrong pane, arrive while input is not accepted, duplicate a still-running request, or corrupt a prompt. Require a unique run/session identity, cooldown, an auditable nudge, and a fresh independent activity signal before escalation. Preserve+kill+relaunch is a reasonable last resort only after quiescing/locking the worktree and proving the prior run is dead; automated commit of uncommitted changes is itself race-prone and must not run concurrently with agent writes. (2) Request-level timeout is the correct root-cause tier if the hang is an unbounded provider stream. It is feasible only if implemented at the actual provider/stream boundary with cancellation propagation, bounded connect/idle/total deadlines, and explicit retry classification. Verify the OpenCode/provider client path rather than assuming AI_RetryError covers this case. Test partial streams, tool calls, non-idempotent operations, cancellation, and duplicate retry behavior; otherwise Tier 1 can create duplicate work or merely move the hang. (3) The >2x expected-interval rule is a useful alert heuristic, not a reliable state transition by itself. ‘Expected interval’ is underspecified and fixed thresholds will false-positive during long compiles/tools, approvals, provider slowness, timer jitter, and sync delays. Use monotonic timestamps, an independent heartbeat/activity contract, phase-specific/adaptive deadlines, and grace periods; require status nonterminal plus stale heartbeat/activity, and record why a run is exempt. File mtimes/commits/comments alone are weak signals because a hung request may have no writes and a slow valid operation may also have none. (4) Main risks are real: relaunch can mask provider/systemic incidents and burn tokens; duplicate agents can race for the same issue/worktree; preserve/commit can capture partial or conflicting state; tmux/process identity can be stale; hydration/sync can observe stale status or race with launch/cleanup; and notifications can be lost. Max-two relaunches limits loops but does not prevent two watchers/runs from acting on the same agent, nor does it define whether the counter is per issue, run, or incident. (5) Missing gates: atomic status schema with run ID and timestamps; single-writer/lease ownership and idempotency keys; recovery ledger recording detection, nudge, kill, relaunch, and operator notification outcomes; launch/kill confirmation and duplicate-run prevention; backoff/jitter and a global concurrency/token budget; explicit handling for human intervention, CI_FAILED, removed worktrees, sync outages, and watcher restart; secure/validated tmux target and command quoting; notification failure escalation; dry-run/manual-approval mode; fault-injection tests for hung streams and slow-but-working agents; and a documented, explicitly approved exception to HALT-on-failure. Recommendation: ship monitor + notify + request-timeout instrumentation first; make nudge/relaunch opt-in or manual until these invariants are demonstrated.

76fc327c-0d50-469d-97f3-f7aac76dc3d8.author: pp3g-yAv3-independent-review-recommend-which-read-only-bash-94ab
76fc327c-0d50-469d-97f3-f7aac76dc3d8.content:
VERDICT: Add the following read-only bash tools to the Orchestrator allowlist, grouped by category:

**Monitoring (distinguish working from stalled):**
1. ps — The playbook (§6.1) explicitly requires `ps -o pid,etime,time,stat -p <pid>` to distinguish stalled from working agents. TIME column climbing = computing; frozen + old heartbeat = stalled. Without ps, the orchestrator cannot detect dead agents. This is the single most critical addition.
2. tmux list-sessions — Kickoff agents run in tmux sessions; the orchestrator must check session liveness. Read-only.
3. tmux list-windows — Check tmux window states for agent health. Read-only.
4. tmux capture-pane — Read agent output from tmux panes for verification. Read-only.
5. tmux display-message — Get tmux server/session info. Read-only.

**Verification:**
6. grep — Search output/logs for error patterns, test results, pass/fail markers. Essential for result validation. Read-only.
7. diff — Compare files/results (e.g., expected vs actual). Essential for verification. Read-only.
8. tail — Read the end of log files and agent output streams. Read-only.
9. head — Read the beginning of files for quick inspection. Read-only.
10. wc — Count lines/words to verify output completeness. Read-only.
11. stat — Check file metadata (timestamps, sizes) to verify artifact freshness. Read-only.

**Coordination across repos:**
No new tools needed — crosslink already handles repo coordination (kickoff/swarm across worktrees, hub branch sync). Adding ssh or curl would introduce mutation risk.

**System health:**
12. free — Memory usage monitoring. Read-only.
13. df — Disk space monitoring. Read-only.
14. uptime — System load/uptime for health checks. Read-only.
15. date — Timestamps for coordination and log correlation. Read-only.

**Verification/debugging:**
16. which — Verify tool availability before delegating. Read-only.
17. env — Display environment for debugging delegation issues. Read-only.

Tools NOT recommended (mutation risk): curl (can POST/write to remote endpoints), ssh (can execute remote commands), sqlite3 (can write to databases), find (can be used with -exec to mutate), kill (mutates process state).

Rationale summary: ps is the #1 priority (playbook explicitly mandates it for stalled-agent detection). tmux subcommands are needed because kickoff agents run in tmux sessions. grep/diff/tail/head/wc/stat form the verification toolkit. free/df/uptime/date cover system health. which/env support debugging. No mutation-risk tools are recommended.

7d33214a-2fc0-471c-886c-734718d52faa.content:
## DELTA RE-REVIEW r2 — VERDICT: AGREE-with-12-specific-findings

I am a fresh reviewer (minimax-m3), not in the first wave. I re-derived the 5 deltas in the FINALIZED synthesis on #241 (23:43 decision comment) from the brief on #251 alone — I have not read other reviewer sub-issues (#250, #252) per the explicit instruction. My verdict is **AGREE on all five deltas in principle, with concrete findings — one of which is potentially load-bearing and should be resolved before canonicalization.** No element fails; no element is unsalvageable.

The principles are correct. The deltas address real failure modes (information-asymmetry blind spots, silent non-delivery, role-boundary crossings). The findings below are clarifications, granularity, and one timing concern — not fundamental disagreements.

---

### Per-delta assessment

#### (a) AUDITOR as divergence verifier — trigger-invoked, read-only, flags to orchestrator
**AGREE.** Trigger-invoked (not always-on) is the right call given audit cost. Read-only preserves the role boundary the cheapest-test-first principle is trying to protect (the auditor must not become a producer). Flagging (not acting) to the orchestrator preserves the single-integration-point invariant (delta c).

**Findings:**
- **A1 (trigger set is under-specified).** The synthesis names the cheap staleness trigger ("heartbeat >2x expected") as a *separate* element, not as the AUDITOR's trigger. The full AUDITOR trigger set needs enumeration. Logical candidates: position staleness; position-vs-artifact claim mismatch (text-claim says "tests pass" but no test run in evidence); reviewer disagreement (split verdicts, 1-of-N catches, disagree values per #241 schema); evidence-accuracy flags from the REVIEWER (delta e); orchestrator-explicit request. Without an enumerated trigger set, AUDITOR is a "heartbeat auditor," not a "divergence auditor."
- **A2 (verification depth per trigger unspecified).** "Joins position claims vs artifact evidence" can mean textual claim-vs-text (cheap structural diff) OR re-derivation (expensive, like hy3's live binary + source re-derivation on #154 R1). The depth matters: cheap catches textual divergence but not semantic divergence (e.g., agent claims "tests pass" and the artifact shows a test run, but the test run was for a different test). The synthesis should specify per-trigger what kind of verification is invoked. Default: cheap structural check first; escalate to re-derivation only on structural mismatch.

#### (b) Position-emitting agents — structured updates to a durable store, task-adaptive cadence
**AGREE.** Structured positions (step/completed/next/blocker + evidence link) match the AGENTS.md workflow contract exactly. Durable store is non-negotiable (positions must survive agent restarts so the AUDITOR can check them after the producer is gone). Task-adaptive cadence is the right call — a 5-minute task should not require 5 checkpoints.

**Findings:**
- **B1 (cadence provenance is under-specified).** "Task-adaptive cadence" raises the question: who sets the cadence? If the agent itself, it can game the cadence (a builder emits fewer positions to reduce audit exposure). The dispatch spec should carry cadence as a parameter set by the orchestrator, OR a default policy (e.g., "every state transition + every Nth minute of idle + at any blocker") should be canonical. The synthesis needs to say where cadence comes from.
- **B2 (position vs status terminology conflation).** "Position" implies a stated claim (e.g., "I claim X is true because Y"). The structure step/completed/next/blocker is status-shaped (current state), not claim-shaped. If positions are claims, the AUDITOR is checking claim-vs-artifact (semantic). If positions are statuses, the AUDITOR is checking status-vs-artifact (syntactic). The two have different semantics and different audit procedures. The design should pick one and name it.
- **B3 (evidence-link canonical form unspecified).** The link is what the AUDITOR and REVIEWER use to verify the claim. If the format is inconsistent (paths, URLs, issue numbers, free text), the divergence check is brittle. A canonical form is needed: e.g., URI to a specific artifact with optional sub-anchor (file:line, test name, commit SHA). The synthesis should specify.
- **B4 (storage form unspecified).** SQLite? Files in a positions dir? Crosslink issues as first-class positions? Each has different durability, query, and cross-agent access properties. Given crosslink is already the durable surface for issue tracking, the natural choice is to make positions first-class crosslink artifacts (or a side-table mirrored from crosslink). This is a strong design choice worth making explicit, not deferring.

#### (c) ORCHESTRATOR as single integration point (sole agent operator deals with)
**AGREE.** This is the strongest of the five deltas. Operator bandwidth is the bottleneck; making the orchestrator the sole contact preserves the operator's mental model and prevents the operator from having to reconcile signals from N independent agents. All other agents' surfaces (AUDITOR flags, REVIEWER verdicts, position updates) flow through the orchestrator.

**Findings:**
- **C1 (orchestrator meta-supervision gap — potentially load-bearing).** The orchestrator now gates: AUDITOR flags, REVIEWER verdicts, position updates, operator commands. If the orchestrator misroutes, misprioritizes, drops a flag, or hangs, no one catches it. The design treats the orchestrator as infallible at the meta level — which is exactly the kind of role-boundary claim the cheapest-test-first principle should apply to. A minimum mitigation: the orchestrator itself emits a heartbeat/position (delta b applies to the orchestrator too), and a sibling agent (or the operator) can audit the orchestrator's flag triage decisions on a sample basis. This is not a fundamental disagreement; it is a recognition that the invariant "orchestrator is sole contact" does not entail "orchestrator is unsupervised."
- **C2 (orchestrator SPOF recovery path missing).** If the orchestrator dies, the operator loses their sole contact. The synthesis does not name a recovery path. A trivial one: orchestrator state is durable (it owns the issue tracker anyway), so a fresh orchestrator can resume from the last known state. But "trivial" is doing work here — the synthesis should make the resumption contract explicit.
- **C3 (orchestrator scope-creep risk).** The orchestrator now does: dispatch, position tracking, flag triage, model-agreement collection, queue-based closeout, decision surfacing. The luna thin-orchestrator-load concern is named, the mitigation is named (bounded flags + queue-based closeout), but the BOUNDARY is not — what does the orchestrator explicitly NOT do? A short explicit list would prevent the orchestrator from absorbing everything.

#### (d) Model-agreement collection with external correctness anchor + non-delivery as first-class outcome
**AGREE on the principles, both load-bearing.** The "external correctness anchor" insight (hy3 F11 — agreement is not truth) is the sharpest element of the design. It is a real correction to a common failure mode: treating high multi-model agreement as evidence. The anchor (test results, type checker, runtime check, formal verification) is the truth criterion; agreement is a confidence multiplier, not a substitute. "Non-delivery as first-class outcome" (hy3 F12) is the parallel correction: 504s, hangs, and timeouts should not be silently masked by re-dispatch; the absence of a verdict is itself a verdict. Both are evidence-anchored (not speculation), which is what the reasoning-certainty principle requires.

**Findings:**
- **D1 (external anchor provenance is unspecified per claim class).** For "tests pass," the anchor is the test runner output. For "type-safe," the type checker. For "documented," a structure check. For "principle-followed" (e.g., "the orchestrator is thin"), there is no test — the anchor is a structural observation by an external agent. The synthesis should enumerate the anchor per claim class in the model-agreement schema (#241 deliverable, C1–C10 taxonomy). Without this, "external anchor" is a label, not a procedure.
- **D2 (non-delivery taxonomy unspecified).** "Non-delivery" is a label; the categories are very different signals: 504 (server-side, harness-related), hang (client-side, agent-related), timeout (policy), refused (auth/policy), broken (mid-task crash), truncated (partial output). Each suggests a different cause and response. First-class status is right; categories need to be named.
- **D3 (anchor and agreement are orthogonal — should be tracked separately, not grouped).** The synthesis groups "external correctness anchor" and "model-agreement collection" under delta (d). They are different primitives: the anchor is verification, the agreement is confidence. They should be recorded as separate columns in the per-wave table (per #241 schema), not collapsed. Grouping in narrative is fine; collapsing in storage is not.
- **D4 (agent-vs-harness source distinction missing).** A 504 may come from the agent (agent hung) or from the harness (gateway overload while calling the agent). The orchestrator must distinguish these — they have different responses (re-dispatch the agent vs page the harness operator). The synthesis should make the source-of-non-delivery explicit.

#### (e) Reviewer = pre-consumption testability audit (L1)
**AGREE on the rename.** Renaming L1 → "testability audit" is a sharp move (per GLM L1/L2/L3 collision finding) and aligns with the cheapest-test-first principle: the reviewer's job is to answer "is there a cheap test that, if it failed, would invalidate the artifact's claims?"

**Findings:**
- **E1 (post-plan cheap test timing — potentially load-bearing concern).** This is the most substantive finding. The first-wave design had three stops: STOP A (post-plan testability audit, L1 cheap), STOP B (pre-consumption result audit), STOP C (targeted L2 re-verification). The finalization's delta (e) collapses STOP A and STOP B into "reviewer = pre-consumption testability audit (L1)." Read literally, this moves the L1 check from post-plan to pre-consumption-of-artifact — i.e., later, not earlier. The cheap early-failure signal is lost: a plan that says "I'll fix file X by editing line N" can be checked at plan-time in seconds (file exists? line content matches? tests exercise line N?) — far cheaper than running the full L1 audit after the artifact is built. If the plan is unworkable, the orchestrator learns this at artifact-time, not plan-time. This is a real cost. **Possible resolution (read into the design, not stated):** STOP A is preserved on the orchestrator side as part of dispatch (the orchestrator reviews the plan as part of accepting it), and the REVIEWER's role is delta (e) — the pre-consumption gate on the artifact. This reading preserves the cheap-test-first principle but requires the synthesis to make it explicit. **The synthesis should disambiguate: is STOP A preserved (orchestrator-side at dispatch) or dropped?**
- **E2 ("testability" is a vague term).** Testable by whom? With what? The cheapest-test-first principle should apply to the reviewer itself. The reviewer's "testability audit" should answer, per claim: is there a cheap discriminating test? If yes, run it. If no, escalate to STOP C (L2 re-verification) or flag to AUDITOR (delta a). The "testability" framing is right; the methodology for "is this testable, and what is the cheapest test?" is missing.
- **E3 (who is the consumer?).** If the orchestrator is the sole consumer (delta c), the reviewer gates the orchestrator. But agents also consume artifacts: a builder consumes a plan; a reviewer consumes a build artifact. Are all of these gated by the reviewer, or only the orchestrator's consumption? The design should specify. My read: the reviewer is the gate on the orchestrator's consumption (the orchestrator consumes the artifact last), and the builder's consumption of the plan is its own self-check (the cheapest-test-first principle applies in the builder's own work).

---

### Summary table

| Delta | Verdict | Findings | Load-bearing? |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) AUDITOR | AGREE | A1 trigger set; A2 verification depth | no |
| (b) Positions | AGREE | B1 cadence provenance; B2 position vs status; B3 evidence-link form; B4 storage form | no |
| (c) Orchestrator | AGREE | C1 meta-supervision; C2 SPOF recovery; C3 scope boundaries | C1 yes |
| (d) Agreement | AGREE | D1 anchor provenance; D2 non-delivery taxonomy; D3 anchor-vs-agreement separation; D4 agent-vs-harness source | no |
| (e) Reviewer | AGREE | E1 STOP A timing; E2 testability methodology; E3 consumer definition | E1 yes |

**Two potentially load-bearing findings: C1 (orchestrator meta-supervision) and E1 (post-plan cheap test timing).** Both have plausible resolutions within the current design; both should be made explicit rather than left implicit.

**Bottom line:** the design is sound, the five deltas are the right shape, the failure modes they target are real and well-evidenced. I do not block canonicalization. I do ask the operator to consider resolving C1 and E1 before treating the design as final, and to address the granularity findings (A1–A2, B1–B4, D1–D4) as the design is implemented.

FINAL ALLOWLIST SPEC (2026-08-03) — synthesized from 3 independent reviewer verdicts (ling #128, big-pickle #130, nemotron #132; laguna #129 failed — silent provider hang) + operator decisions + thin-orchestrator token-budget principle.

ACCEPT (scoped): ps (targeted 'ps -o pid,etime,time,stat -p <pid>' form), pgrep, tmux (list-sessions / capture-pane with small scrollback -S -20 / display-message), grep (discipline: always pipe to head/tail), tail (bounded forms e.g. tail -50), head (bounded forms e.g. head -50), wc, stat, diff, free, df, which, date, uptime, env (discipline: selective 'env | grep FOO' only; NEVER paste raw output to shared channels), git worktree list (scoped), git -C (scoped read-only compact: status / log --oneline / diff --stat / show --stat), curl -I / curl --head only (headers, no body, no POST).

ACCEPTED WITH DELEGATION RULE: git log --oneline, git diff --stat, git show --stat (compact forms only; deep diff review = Reviewer's job).

REJECT: find (mutation flags -delete/-exec), awk/sed (sed -i edits files), less (redundant with head/tail), blanket git log/diff/show (unbounded output), curl body/POST, any git write.

NEW PLAYBOOK RULE (thin orchestrator): The orchestrator consumes bounded signals only. Any read requiring large volume (whole files, full diffs, log analysis) is DELEGATED to a subagent which returns a summary. Never paste large raw output into the orchestrator context or a shared channel. Rationale: orchestrator context is the scarcest resource; same principle as webfetch:deny on orchestrator while subagents have fetch.

APPLY TO BOTH REPOS (ASES + tripn-astro) per two-repo sync rule (playbook 5.5): .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md frontmatter bash map AND .crosslink/hook-config.json allowed_bash_prefixes, plus the new playbook rule in agent-orchestration-playbook.md.

6070f165-b325-4371-9051-efae52aa2dec.content:
# DESIGN: Durable opencode silent-hang fix (#154) — design sketch

**Sub-issue**: #175 · **Parent**: #154 · **Epic**: #156
**Designer**: Builder pp3g-i81g (design-only task; no code or binary changes made)
**Date**: 2026-08-04

---

## 0. Current-state finding (verified this session — changes the urgency)

**The installed opencode was upgraded `1.18.11 → 1.18.12` at `2026-08-04 03:15:59`, silently wiping the #145 emergency binary patch.** Verified in the live binary:

- Installed: `/home/claude-code/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.3/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe` reports `opencode --version` = `1.18.12`, size `179,349,632` bytes, mtime `2026-08-04 03:15:59`.
- The #145 marker `if(false)return` appears **0 times**; the original guard `if(!$.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/event-stream"))return $;` is back at offset `97992552`.
- `sst/opencode` resolves via GitHub 301 redirect to `anomalyco/opencode`; tags `v1.18.11` and `v1.18.12` both exist; `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` is **byte-identical** between the two tags (2011 lines, `rtk diff` = identical).

**Consequence**: the silent-hang bug described in #144 is LIVE again as of this morning's upgrade. The durable fix is not hypothetical — it is the only protection until an upstream PR (#39516 / #35743) lands. This design is the durable replacement for the wiped interim patch.

---

## 1. Fork strategy

### 1.1 Naming reconciliation (sst/opencode vs anomalyco/opencode)

**Verdict: `sst/opencode` and `anomalyco/opencode` are the SAME repository — the repo was renamed; GitHub serves a 301 redirect from the old name.**

Evidence (verified this session):
- `gh api repos/sst/opencode` returns `full_name: "anomalyco/opencode"`.
- `curl -sI https://github.com/sst/opencode` → `HTTP/2 301` → `location: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode`.
- `gh api repos/anomalyco/opencode/tags` lists both `v1.18.11` and `v1.18.12`; release `v1.18.11` published `2026-08-01`.
- The #145 claim "binary matches sst/opencode @ v1.18.11" is consistent: the tag `v1.18.11` on the canonical repo matches the embedded source (the extracted `provider.ts.orig` is byte-identical to the canonical v1.18.11 file).
- The #145 upstream comments correctly went to `anomalyco/opencode` (issue #26487, PR #39516) — that is the canonical, current name.

**Canonical upstream**: `anomalyco/opencode` (formerly `sst/opencode`; the old name is a redirect and should not be used for new clones/remotes).

### 1.2 Fork + pin

- **Create a fork of `anomalyco/opencode`** (project-owned; e.g. under the same org as this repo).
- **Pin the fork at tag `v1.18.12`** — the version currently installed and the npm package version (`opencode-ai@1.18.12`), so `opencode --version` stays coherent with the managed package. NOTE: issue text says "v1.18.11" (correct when written); `provider.ts` is byte-identical between v1.18.11 and v1.18.12, so the same one-line patch applies verbatim to either tag. Pinning v1.18.12 avoids a version-skew (npm says 1.18.12, binary reports 1.18.11).
- **Track the patch as a committed divergence on the fork** (one commit: `fix(provider): apply body-read deadline to all responses`), keeping a clean rebase path against upstream tags. Same pattern as the crosslink fork documented in `.crosslink/knowledge/crosslink-fork.md`.

### 1.3 How the fix survives opencode upgrades

The upgrade vector: `opencode upgrade` / `npm install -g opencode-ai@latest` replaces the npm-managed `bin/opencode.exe` (verified: today's 1.18.12 upgrade did exactly this, wiping the patch). Survival design (layered):

1. **Primary — launch-chain indirection.** Install the fork-built binary at a durable, npm-independent path, e.g. `~/.local/opencode-fork/bin/opencode.exe`, and change the `REAL` variable in the `~/.local/bin/opencode` wrapper to point at it. The launch chain (`crosslink kickoff → tmux → claude wrapper → opencode`) uses the wrapper, so future `opencode upgrade` / npm updates of the stock package rewrite only the npm-managed binary and **cannot** touch the fork binary. The wrapper's models-cache rewrite runs against the fork binary unchanged.
2. **Secondary — disable self-update.** Set `"autoupdate": false` in the global config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) so the built-in updater (`packages/opencode/src/cli/upgrade.ts`: `if (config.autoupdate === false || Flag.OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE) return`) never silently replaces the binary. Optionally set `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1`.
3. **Tertiary — documented re-apply procedure.** `.crosslink/knowledge/opencode-fork.md` (mirrors `crosslink-fork.md`) records: canonical upstream identity, pinned tag, patch, build steps, and the invariant "any deliberate upgrade = rebuild fork at new tag, re-apply patch, re-run install steps". See §5.4.

---

## 2. Exact patch (source-level diff)

File: `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` (canonical @ v1.18.12; identical @ v1.18.11). Two hunks.

### Hunk 1 — `wrapSSE` region (lines 37–82): keep SSE per-chunk wrapper; ADD a non-SSE total-completion wrapper

**Replace the guard-only removal with a dispatcher + `wrapBody` (design requirement 3).**

```diff
 const OPENAI_HEADER_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 300_000
+const DEFAULT_BODY_TIMEOUT = 1_800_000 // 30 min, non-SSE body-completion deadline
 
 function wrapSSE(res: Response, ms: number, ctl: AbortController) {
   if (typeof ms !== "number" || ms <= 0) return res
   if (!res.body) return res
-  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/event-stream")) return res
 
   const reader = res.body.getReader()
   const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
     async pull(ctrl) {
       const part = await new Promise<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof reader.read>>>((resolve, reject) => {
         const id = setTimeout(() => {
           const err = new ProviderError.ResponseStreamError("SSE read timed out")
           ctl.abort(err)
           void reader.cancel(err)
           reject(err)
         }, ms)
 
         reader.read().then(
           (part) => {
             clearTimeout(id)
             resolve(part)
           },
           (err) => {
             clearTimeout(id)
             reject(err)
           },
         )
       })
 
       if (part.done) {
         ctrl.close()
         return
       }
 
       ctrl.enqueue(part.value)
     },
     async cancel(reason) {
       ctl.abort(reason)
       await reader.cancel(reason)
     },
   })
 
   return new Response(body, {
     headers: new Headers(res.headers),
     status: res.status,
     statusText: res.statusText,
   })
 }
+
+// NEW: total body-completion deadline for non-SSE responses.
+// The deadline is a single timer for the WHOLE body: it fires only if the body
+// does not complete within `ms`, never on slow-but-progressing chunks.
+// This preserves the original guard's intent (do not abort slow-but-legitimate
+// non-streaming bodies, hy3 F2) while still killing a body that never closes.
+function wrapBody(res: Response, ms: number, ctl: AbortController) {
+  if (typeof ms !== "number" || ms <= 0) return res
+  if (!res.body) return res
+  const reader = res.body.getReader()
+  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
+    async start(ctrl) {
+      const id = setTimeout(() => {
+        const err = new ProviderError.ResponseStreamError("Body read timed out")
+        ctl.abort(err)
+        void reader.cancel(err)
+        ctrl.error(err)
+      }, ms)
+      try {
+        for (;;) {
+          const { done, value } = await reader.read()
+          if (done) {
+            clearTimeout(id)
+            ctrl.close()
+            return
+          }
+          ctrl.enqueue(value)
+        }
+      } catch (e) {
+        clearTimeout(id)
+        ctrl.error(e instanceof Error ? e : new Error(String(e)))
+      }
+    },
+    async cancel(reason) {
+      ctl.abort(reason)
+      await reader.cancel(reason)
+    },
+  })
+  return new Response(body, {
+    headers: new Headers(res.headers),
+    status: res.status,
+    statusText: res.statusText,
+  })
+}
```

### Hunk 2 — `resolveSDK` fetch wrapper (lines ~1736–1767): dispatch on content-type

```diff
         const customFetch = options["fetch"]
         const chunkTimeout = options["chunkTimeout"]
         const headerTimeout = options["headerTimeout"]
+        const bodyTimeout = options["bodyTimeout"] ?? DEFAULT_BODY_TIMEOUT
         delete options["chunkTimeout"]
         delete options["headerTimeout"]
+        delete options["bodyTimeout"]
 
         options["fetch"] = async (input: any, init?: BunFetchRequestInit) => {
           const fetchFn = customFetch ?? fetch
           const opts = init ?? {}
           const chunkAbortCtl = typeof chunkTimeout === "number" && chunkTimeout > 0 ? new AbortController() : undefined
+          const bodyAbortCtl = typeof bodyTimeout === "number" && bodyTimeout > 0 ? new AbortController() : undefined
           const headerTimeoutMs = headerTimeout === false ? undefined : headerTimeout
           const headerTimeoutCtl = typeof headerTimeoutMs === "number" ? timeoutController(headerTimeoutMs) : undefined
           const signals: AbortSignal[] = []
 
           if (opts.signal) signals.push(opts.signal)
           if (chunkAbortCtl) signals.push(chunkAbortCtl.signal)
+          if (bodyAbortCtl) signals.push(bodyAbortCtl.signal)
           if (headerTimeoutCtl) signals.push(headerTimeoutCtl.signal)
           if (options["timeout"] !== undefined && options["timeout"] !== null && options["timeout"] !== false)
             signals.push(AbortSignal.timeout(options["timeout"]))
 
           const combined = signals.length === 0 ? null : signals.length === 1 ? signals[0] : AbortSignal.any(signals)
           if (combined) opts.signal = combined
 
           const res = await fetchFn(input, {
             ...opts,
             // @ts-ignore see here: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/16682
             timeout: false,
           }).finally(() => headerTimeoutCtl?.clear())
 
-          if (!chunkAbortCtl) return res
-          return wrapSSE(res, chunkTimeout, chunkAbortCtl)
+          const isSSE = res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/event-stream")
+          if (isSSE) {
+            if (!chunkAbortCtl) return res
+            return wrapSSE(res, chunkTimeout, chunkAbortCtl)
+          }
+          if (!bodyAbortCtl) return res
+          return wrapBody(res, bodyTimeout, bodyAbortCtl)

```

**Note on the emergency fallback**: the #145 one-liner (delete the guard line only, so `chunkTimeout` wraps all bodies) is the *minimal* variant of this same patch. The design's recommended durable form is the dispatcher above, which is strictly safer (see §3). The fork should carry the dispatcher; the one-liner exists in git history for emergency re-use.

---

## 3. Non-SSE deadline design — decision + rationale

**Decision: OPTION B — add a distinct, longer body-completion deadline for non-SSE responses. Do NOT relax the guard to apply `chunkTimeout` (per-chunk idle timeout) to all bodies.**

| | Option A: relax guard entirely | Option B (RECOMMENDED): distinct body-completion deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Non-SSE hang (application/json never closes) | killed after chunkTimeout | killed after bodyTimeout (longer, still bounded) |
| Slow-but-legitimate non-SSE body (hy3 F2) | **false-aborted** when any inter-chunk gap > chunkTimeout | **preserved** — only a body that NEVER completes is aborted |
| Semantics | per-chunk idle timeout applied to non-streaming bodies (semantically wrong) | total body-completion deadline (semantically correct for non-SSE) |
| Regression risk (luna #150 / hy3 #153 F2) | HIGH (untested slow-non-SSE regression) | LOW (original intent retained) |
| Changes to SSE path | none | none |
| Code | one-line deletion | ~30 lines (dispatcher + wrapBody), reviewed below |

**Rationale** (converges with the 4-reviewer consensus #150–#153 and the #154 requirements):
1. hy3 F2 is the specific failure the reviewers flagged: a legitimate non-SSE body with a gap > `chunkTimeout` between chunks would be aborted under Option A. With `chunkTimeout=300000` in prod this is unlikely for typical JSON, but it is a real behavioral regression vs. the original design intent and is untested by the #145 verification table.
2. The non-SSE failure mode is a body that never completes — a *total-completion* deadline is the precise guard for that. A per-chunk idle timeout is the right guard for SSE (streams must keep producing), not for a single-shot body.
3. `wrapBody` starts ONE timer and clears it only on `done`; it cannot false-fire on a slow-but-steady body. This directly implements "preserve original intent of not aborting slow-but-legitimate non-streaming bodies" (#154 requirement 2).
4. Config surface: new provider option `bodyTimeout` (default `DEFAULT_BODY_TIMEOUT`, recommended `1_800_000` = 30 min — generous for legit slow bodies, well under the 1h outer `timeout`, so the body deadline fires first with a descriptive error instead of a generic overall timeout). `chunkTimeout` semantics for SSE are unchanged.
5. `headerTimeout` behavior untouched (no-headers case still surfaces 4 visible `ProviderHeaderTimeoutError` entries, per #144 row 3).

**Explicit trade-off**: non-SSE bodies that legitimately take > 30 min to fully deliver would now be aborted (they were never bounded before). This is acceptable and configurable via `bodyTimeout`; it is the price of killing the 10.9h hang signature.

---

## 4. Error surfacing + retry budget — where and how

### 4.1 Root cause (verified in v1.18.12 source)

- The chunkTimeout abort rejects with `ProviderError.ResponseStreamError("SSE read timed out")` (`provider.ts` wrapSSE; wrapBody will do the same with "Body read timed out").
- `MessageV2.fromError` (`packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts` ~line 626) maps `ResponseStreamError` → `APIError { isRetryable: true }`.
- `SessionRetry.retryable()` (`packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts`) returns a retry payload for any retryable APIError.
- `SessionRetry.policy()` uses **`Schedule.fromStepWithMetadata` — an UNBOUNDED schedule** (no `Schedule.recurs`, no max-attempt cap). Every failure that `retryable()` deems retryable schedules another attempt forever.
- `SessionProcessor.process` (`packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` ~line 660) wraps the LLM stream in `Effect.retry(SessionRetry.policy({...}))` → the silent infinite retry loop with exponential backoff (observed gaps ~3.5/5/7/11/19/33s in #144).
- The **visible ERROR path already exists but is unreachable today**: when `Effect.retry` eventually gives up, `Effect.catch(halt)` runs `halt()` (~line 600) which does `Effect.logError("process", ...)` + publishes `Session.Event.Error` + sets `assistantMessage.error` + status idle. Because the schedule never gives up, zero ERROR entries ever appear.

### 4.2 Design

1. **Cap the retry schedule** in `packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts`:
   - Add `RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (recommended default **3**: initial + 2 retries; configurable via provider option `retry.maxAttempts` or env).
   - In `policy()`'s step, return `Cause.done(meta.attempt)` when `meta.attempt > RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` — the identical stop mechanism `retryable()` already uses for non-retryable errors.
2. **Visible retryable ERROR entry**: with the cap, the chunkTimeout/bodyTimeout abort now flows: abort → `ResponseStreamError` → `APIError{isRetryable:true}` → 2 retries with backoff → schedule gives up → `halt()` → `Effect.logError` ERROR entry + `Session.Event.Error` + message error + status idle. The agent loop sees a real error and the flag stops lying as RUNNING.
3. **Retry budget**: 3 attempts total (≈ initial + 2× backoff ≈ 2s+4s = ~6s of retry before terminal error in the no-headers case; with `retry-after` headers the budget still caps the number of attempts, not the delay). This bounds the previously infinite loop while keeping resilience for genuinely transient provider hiccups.
4. **Distinct timeout messages** ("SSE read timed out" vs "Body read timed out") so logs distinguish the path; both carry `metadata.code = ProviderResponseStreamError` via the existing `MessageV2.fromError` mapping.
5. **Relationship to #146**: with ERROR surfacing + budget, the #135/#146 watcher kill/restart remains the outer safety net for *other* failure modes; it is no longer the only recovery for this one.

513f0126-abff-4948-8d6b-65e8927ba3a1.title: RESEARCH (output-schema drift): cached-manifest output_schema vs live-backend content mismatch as a hard-failure mode for identifier-first tool-calling
513f0126-abff-4948-8d6b-65e8927ba3a1.description:
Follow-on from #196 (ToolRegistry lazy-MCP validation). Flagged by BOTH re-reviewers (hy3 #199 SHOULD-CONSIDER; big-pickle #205) as the most consequential open question for the identifier-first proposal.

THE PROBLEM: mcp/client/session.py:1096-1100 — when a listed tool DOES declare an output_schema, call_tool raises RuntimeError if the result carries no conforming structured content. In a lazy-proxy design the schema comes from the CACHED MANIFEST while the content comes from the LIVE BACKEND — so manifest-to-backend schema drift is a hard-failure mode intrinsic to the identifier-first architecture. It was NEVER exercised: manifest.json:30 sets output_schema: null, so the current evidence does not cover this path.

SCOPE (when dispatched — the operator will provide the full draft brief to the agent): investigate whether a cached-manifest proxy can survive tools that declare output schemas, what drift does at runtime, and whether it requires a richer proxy (schema-aware forwarding) or a ToolRegistry-side change. Evidence-only task, consistent with #196. Do NOT re-run the #196 tests wholesale; this is a new focused investigation.

1e6dc62d-32e7-4aa7-8771-94d65c6e6556.content:
Result: output-schema drift characterization complete (evidence-only; no mitigation built). New sibling dir research/toolregistry-lazy-mcp/output-schema-drift/ committed at cd5011c (scaffolding + 8 phase tests + logs + report.md).

All tests A-F passed (plus supplementary C2/C3). Central claim CONFIRMED: drift is only detectable after the backend is spawned AND responds (Test C: first spawn 2484ms after call invocation, drift detected only after backend_up + forward + response-validation, caller-visible failure at 6.0-7.3s normal load; worst observed 23.7s under machine load with backend init 3.2-4.2s).

Key findings:
- Test A (null schema): non-conforming {"result": n} shape succeeds — the C/D contrast baseline. Test B (matching schema): clean success 1810-3124ms.
- Test C (backend still declares conforming schema, returns diverging shape): caller sees MCPError (NOT RuntimeError) — the RuntimeError fires inside the proxy's own client (validates against the backend's LIVE schema), is converted to a JSON-RPC error with the schema text preserved. Failure trips BOTH retry layers: proxy-internal respawn + ToolRegistry reconnect-retry (connection.py:106) → 4 backend spawns + 2 persistent proxies per failed call, 0 retries succeed.
- Test C2 (backend drifted consistently, only cached manifest stale): RuntimeError surfaces DIRECTLY (exact session.py:1096-1100 mechanism), 2 backend spawns, and the SDK's cache-miss re-list is a no-op (re-absorbs the same stale cached schema).
- Test C3 (bare number): fails even earlier — backend's own response serialization rejects structured_content=5.0 for protocol 2025-11-25 → opaque MCPError(-32603, 'Handler returned an invalid result').
- Test D: input proven valid against cached input schema; validate-before-spawn lets the call through and cannot prevent this failure mode.
- Test E: deterministic — immediate repeat fails identically, paying the full double-retry cost again (8 spawns total). NO recovery/refresh mechanism exists in ToolRegistry (grep: zero), the proxy (static manifest), the SDK's cache-miss re-list (served from the same stale manifest), or the repo (no Lexicon-CID path anywhere).
- Test F: blast radius contained — unrelated multiply succeeds in the same session (923-1335ms), discovery intact, failing tool keeps failing. Note: multiply still pays a fresh backend spawn because the failed call closed the proxy's backend session.

Wasted cost: drift failure ≈ 2.3x the successful-with-schema baseline (C≈2.3x B by midpoint), 4 spawns + 1 extra proxy + 3-5s over a successful cold call, per attempt, repeating deterministically.

Conclusion (recommendation, not built): NOT an acceptable bounded cost — requires a mitigation (periodic manifest revalidation or fallback live-schema fetch on mismatch; the backend is already running when the mismatch is found, so a fallback re-list is cheap).

Versions pinned: toolregistry 0.15.0, mcp 2.0.0, python 3.10.12 (venv reused). Full detail + log index: report.md

020611f8-0a09-4780-a9ac-39938f347a29.content:
Plan: Fix watchdog exit-condition bug in fork launch.rs build_watchdog_script (line 100). The current check 'if [ -f {worktree}/.kickoff-status ]; then exit 0; fi' disarms the watchdog as soon as the status file exists — and launch.rs writes LAUNCHING (line 648) BEFORE spawn_watchdog (line 670), so the watchdog always exits on its first check and the heartbeat-staleness nudge logic is dead code.

Approach (option 1 from the issue): change the exit condition from file EXISTENCE to TERMINAL CONTENT. The script will read .kickoff-status and exit 0 only when its content starts with a terminal marker (DONE / FAILED / CI_FAILED / TIMEOUT — matching the existing conventions in sentinel/collect.rs classify_status and pipeline.rs probe_run_worktree). Non-terminal content (LAUNCHING / RUNNING / empty) continues to the heartbeat staleness + tmux send-keys nudge path, preserving existing behavior.

Scope: fork repo /home/claude-code/projects/crosslink, file crosslink/src/commands/kickoff/launch.rs + regression tests in crosslink/src/commands/kickoff/tests.rs. No hydration/hub files touched (#142 isolation). Add functional regression tests that execute the generated script: (a) terminal status DONE/FAILED/CI_FAILED => exit 0 with no nudge sent; (b) RUNNING status + stale heartbeat => nudge fires (proves script no longer exits on mere file existence). Rebuild per crosslink-fork.md (cargo install --path ... --force with lld).

## REVIEW (2/3): Root cause assessment — #109 CONFIRMED, but the investigation plan is incomplete

### Q2: Is #109 correctly identified as the root cause? Is the approach sound?

VERDICT: The defect is REAL and I reproduced it live in this session. But the denial-origin trace as scoped is missing a critical branch, and fixing #109 in isolation would open a security hole.

LIVE REPRODUCTION: This session runs under .opencode/agents/reviewer.md (frontmatter l.7-14: bash map declaring crosslink/git/ls/cat/cargo/npm allow). The effective permission rules shown to me declare 'git *' and 'ls *' and 'cat *' as ALLOWED — yet every git/ls/cat call is denied; only 'crosslink *' executes. KICKOFF.md's 'Always allowed: git status, git diff...' list is false in practice. This matches #109 exactly.

DENIAL-ORIGIN MAP (new evidence — the plan must account for all four layers):
1. .opencode/plugins/crosslink-guard.ts is NOT LOADED. Neither the repo .opencode/opencode.json nor the global ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json reference it (global plugin array = ./plugins/plugin.ts + ./plugins/interrupt.ts; the global plugin.ts only configures providers). So the plugin's blocked-git and allowed-bash logic is dead code in the current environment.
2. .claude/hooks/*.py are NOT deployed (crosslink workflow diff lists all 6 missing). .claude/settings.json invokes them with 'if [ -f HOOK ]; then ... else exit 0' — silent fail-open. So NO git-mutation enforcement, NO heartbeat.
3. The actual denials come from opencode's built-in permission matcher over the frontmatter-derived rules — and the matcher contradicts its own displayed rules (allows listed, deny applied). This is either an opencode matcher bug/version issue (possibly OUTSIDE repo control) or a frontmatter syntax problem (the 'deny' + specific-allow map form may not be interpreted the way it reads).
4. crosslink kickoff also constructs --allowedTools at launch (config kickoff.allowed_tools is unset); the launcher's construction may override frontmatter. This is the 'build_allowed_tools' lead in #109 — keep it, but it is not the only suspect.

MUST FIX — Security-relevant sequencing hole: today the ONLY thing blocking git push/merge/reset/clean for read-only agents is the blanket bash deny. The frontmatter declares 'git *' allow, which INCLUDES git push. If #109 simply makes the permission layer honor 'git *', read-only agents become git-write-capable with no enforcement layer left (plugin unloaded, hooks missing). #109 must pair the permission fix with deploying an enforcement layer (load crosslink-guard.ts and/or deploy the hooks) — or choose deny-bash-and-rewrite-docs. The plan must add this, and the verification criterion must include 'git push remains blocked for reviewer/auditor'.

SOUNDNESS of the proposed investigation: the trace direction is right, but drop the crosslink-guard.ts hypothesis early (it is not loaded — unless the plan intends to load it, which is itself a scope decision). First cheap discriminator: test whether the deny persists with a minimal frontmatter (bash: allow like builder.md, which reportedly worked in prior AC-1 runs) vs the map form — if the map form is the trigger, the fix is config syntax, not the matcher.

ALSO NOTE: #109's claim that hook-config declares cat/grep/find allowed is inaccurate — hook-config.json allowed_bash_prefixes omits cat/grep/find (they exist only in the plugin's DEFAULT_ALLOWED_BASH, which hook-config REPLACES). The 'declared allowed' sources are mutually inconsistent: hook-config allows ls/dir/pwd/echo/git-status..., frontmatter allows git/ls/cat/cargo/npm..., KICKOFF.md promises git read-only. Reconciling all three is part of the fix.

## REVIEW (3/3): Gaps + Wave 3 design — the final gate is right in principle, under-specified in practice

### Q3: Gaps — missing fixes, risks, steps that belong in the plan

1. MUST FIX — Artifact handoff mechanism is UNDEFINED (the biggest Wave 3 gap). KICKOFF.md states 'Cross-worktree filesystem access is blocked'. AC-1's test-output.txt lives in the builder worktree; reviewer/auditor worktrees cannot reach it. The re-run must specify the mechanism: (a) shared /tmp path (builder frontmatter allows /tmp; prior cycles used /tmp artifacts successfully), or (b) git-based handoff (commit artifact + git fetch . branch + git show) — but note git fetch is NOT in any allowed list today, so option (b) requires the #109 fix to cover it. Then the re-run must prove DOWNSTREAM CONSUMPTION: the reviewer must assert on the artifact content, not a self-contained check (the exact sidestep #118's audit flagged).

2. MUST FIX — Wave 3 PASS criteria are undefined. Closing #78 needs explicit criteria: original AC-1..AC-4 PLUS (i) artifact handoff demonstrated with downstream consumption; (ii) dependency edges present (#111) AND launch-time behavior verified — I found NO evidence that kickoff/swarm enforces blocked_by at launch (the crosslink-guide skill documents 'ready' as advisory; #106-#108 all currently list as ready). If enforcement is process-only, the plan must say so and verify the edges instead of claiming machine enforcement; (iii) all 3 phases post plan+result comments per #117; (iv) auditor completes.

3. MUST FIX — Model selection + timeout for Wave 3 unspecified. North Mini free looped 31 min without completing; big-pickle completed the audit in ~8 min. Pin models for the re-run (e.g., ling/nemotron for builder/reviewer, big-pickle for auditor) or define an explicit max-runtime and failure criterion, else the gate can stall on model lottery.

4. SHOULD CONSIDER — Use FRESH phase issues for the re-run, not #106-#108: they carry prior comments/history, and reusing them invites the duplicate-plan confusion #115 is meant to fix. New issues should bake in the artifact path, dependency edges, and parent #78 link at creation.

5. SHOULD CONSIDER — 'Hooks not deployed' (audit finding #6) has no home in the plan. It contributes to stale-lock misdetection (no heartbeat) and zero git-mutation enforcement. Fold it into #112 or #109.

6. SHOULD CONSIDER — #116 scope misses the invalid 'crosslink comment' form: KICKOFF.md step 4 ('crosslink comment 78 ...' — confirmed: unrecognized subcommand), .crosslink/rules/global.md l.130/l.196, .crosslink/rules/tracking-normal.md l.60. Fix along with the 'crosslink intervene' references.

7. SHOULD CONSIDER — Findings persistence (#114) interacts with Wave 3: if the auditor posts observations but findings docs still don't exist, the documented two-stage consolidation cannot run. Either include a consolidation step in Wave 3 or explicitly scope it out. And #73/#74 must be merged (or their docs cherry-picked) BEFORE #113 closes them.

8. NIT — #118's description names only #109+#111 as preconditions; it should also require the Wave 2 template fixes (#115/#116/#117), since the re-run agents will follow KICKOFF.md.

### Q4: Is Wave 3 (artifact handoff + dependency enforcement) the right final gate?

VERDICT: Right gate, wrong execution unit. Keeping #78 open until a real 3-phase run completes is correct and directly addresses the premature-PASS lesson. But as scoped, #118 inherits the exact failure mode it was created to prevent: without a defined handoff mechanism, defined PASS criteria, pinned models, and a decision on whether 'dependency enforcement' is machine or process, the re-run can again validate three independent agents and be declared PASS. The gate is only honest once items 1-3 above are specified in the plan.

### NOTABLE POSITIVES
- The plan correctly puts the sandbox defect first — it poisoned diagnosis (3 AC-3 failures misattributed to models) and blocks every read-only phase.
- Sub-issue decomposition maps 1:1 to the audit's recommendations; every file:line target in #114/#116 that I checked is accurate.
- #113's --no-changelog discipline and #112's lock cleanup are the right housekeeping, and the wave ordering 0→1→2→3 is sound on the critical path.
- The plan honestly surfaces its own open decision (align vs deny bash) rather than hiding it.

Bottom line: approve the direction; rework #109 to include enforcement deployment + the align/deny decision point, add the handoff mechanism + PASS criteria + model pinning to #118, and re-sequence #113 after #112 with explicit exclusions. Then the re-run is a credible gate.
